# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 13 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 13 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_013_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 5

**1** After I had written the book as I had been instructed in the earlier vision, the Spirit of God took me up and carried me to a trackless region. **2** At once the Spirit was transformed, and I could see the tower clearly; surrounding it were twelve mountains, each with a different character and appearance. **3** The first mountain was black as soot. The second was bare, without any vegetation. The third was overgrown with thorns and briars. The fourth had mixed vegetation — some green, some withered at the tips. The fifth had green grass but was rocky and rugged. The sixth was full of ravines and clefts, some larger and some smaller. The seventh was a cheerful and pleasant mountain — entirely flourishing — where all kinds of animals and birds grazed and fed; the more they fed, the more the vegetation grew. The eighth mountain was full of springs, and every kind of creature the Lord made drank from those springs. **4** The ninth had no water at all — a complete wilderness infested with wild beasts and deadly serpents that killed people. The tenth had great trees and was entirely covered in shade; sheep lay resting and ruminating in that shade. The eleventh was densely covered with trees bearing various kinds of fruit — whoever ate was left wanting more. The twelfth was entirely white, and its appearance was radiant with joy.

---

*LOGOS note: The twelve mountains parallel the twelve tribes of Israel and the twelve apostles — likely intentional. The catalog moves from worst (black/soot) to best (entirely white).*
